titles.title: RedAlert2
titles.engine:
Westwood 2D DirectDraw engine, always 16 bpp.
- Red Alert 2 1.006: game.exe, md5 282f160e...
- Yuri's Revenge 1.001: gamemd.exe, md5 03452ffd...
- Both start through the Ra2.exe / RA2MD.exe stubs.
- gamemd.exe differs from gamemd.old in 14 byte runs (re-counted with cmp). None is in the list builders, the options constructor or loader, or the mode enumerator.
- The game-local aqrit ddraw.dll (27,136 B, PE subsystem 4.0) is a pass-through proxy. It re-exports the DirectDraw entry points and has no EnumDisplayModes code.
- aqrit.cfg sets ForceDirectDrawEmulation=1 on XP. On Vista+ the launcher copies in _win7\aqrit.cfg, which sets it to 0.
titles.launch_sets:
Gameplay runs at 1920x1080x16 on all four LCD boxes.
- Mechanism: both launchers CALL FLEETRES.BAT, then run FLEETRES.EXE -ini RA2.INI / RA2MD.INI Video ScreenWidth %FR_W% and ScreenHeight %FR_H%. This is WritePrivateProfileString, so other keys survive. gameres.h:743-746 write the same values at sync.
- The deployed ra2.ini is byte-identical on .123, .145 and .240 (md5 8d9f9fec...): ScreenWidth=1920, ScreenHeight=1080, and no AllowHiResModes.
- Measured today: while RA2 ran, DISPLAYCFG get read 1920x1080 at 16 bpp on both .145 and .240.
- The main shell is a fixed 800x600 surface centred at (560,240). That is expected.
- The prior agent's .240 caveat (no EDID, next launch falls back to 1024x768) is stale. GAMERES on .240 at 00:40 reports EDID DELL E2313H, persisted and live desktop 1920x1080, and a wide target of 1920x1080.
titles.menu_source:
The list comes from the driver, filtered in code. Confirmed on hardware.
- Path: main menu -> Options (dialog 213) -> 'Set Game Resolution' drop-down (ctrl 1773).
- Fill: IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes (flags 0) through the helper at 0x4962a0. A mode is kept only if dwRGBBitCount (desc+0x54) is 16 and 640x480 <= mode <= max. Entries are labelled '%d x %d x 16'.
- Filter: with [Video] AllowHiResModes=yes the max is 4096x4096. Otherwise the max is 1024x768 and only widths 640, 800 and 1024 pass.
- The constructor at 0x5d8840 sets the flag to 0. Only the loader at 0x5d8de0 reads it (the sole xref to the string), so the game never writes it. Neither staged ini carries it.
- Seen on .145 today: the drop-down listed exactly 640x480x16, 800x600x16 and 1024x768x16. Its current-value box was blank, because the running 1920x1080 mode is filtered out.
- DirectDraw on that same box does enumerate 1920x1080x16.

Correct as proposed, and now hardware-verified on .145 with a temporary ini (the RA2 test above).

Library change:
1. Add AllowHiResModes=yes under [Video] in the staged ra2.ini and RA2MD.INI.
2. Add launcher lines "%~dp0FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%~dp0RA2.INI" Video AllowHiResModes yes, and the same for RA2MD.INI. They must go in as a stage-fleetres.py 'fix' repair pair: patch_launcher() returns early when the launcher already contains the FLEETRES call (MARK), as both launchers do.
3. Add gameres.h rows {RedAlert2, GR_OP_INI, RA2.INI/RA2MD.INI, Video, AllowHiResModes, yes}.
4. Add a staging test that pins those lines. test_gameres_mirror only checks file names.
5. Correct the RedAlert2 recipe comment at stage-fleetres.py:1108-1110. It says the aqrit wrapper 'lets the Westwood engine take a mode its own menu never offers'. In fact the engine reads ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight from the ini itself, and the wrapper has no mode code.
6. Record the menu fact in PER-TITLE-STATUS.md.
7. Then purge and GAMESYNC RedAlert2 on every box, per the staged-game loop.

The staged ini alone would be enough, because the game keeps the key. Steps 2-3 follow the Tiberian Sun precedent as a safeguard.
titles.fix_source: Already in the tree. AllowHiResModes is a stock engine key, read by game.exe at 0x5d8de0 and gamemd.exe at 0x5fa943. Nothing needs downloading. Do not mix in the legacy cnc-ddraw stack at Utility/Retro Automation/ra2-opt.
titles.fix_risk:
Low.
- The flag only widens the Options list and is read nowhere else.
- Westwood's INI writer keeps a key it reads but never writes. Observed today on Tiberian Sun: the game rewrote SUN.INI, adding [Intro] PlaySide00/01, and AllowHiResModes=yes and VideoBackBuffer survived (EVR/240_SUN.INI.before and .after). RA2 uses the same INIClass.
- An in-game mode pick lasts until the next launch, because the launcher rewrites ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight. GAMERES also rewrites them at sync.
- The launcher and GAMERES would both write 'yes', so they cannot fight.
- LAN is unaffected. Resolution is local to each client, and WOLLimitResolution applies only to Westwood Online. Mixed 1080p and 1024x768 peers already play two-box.
- On a CRT box the list simply shows that driver's 16-bpp modes.

titles.title: StarCraft
titles.engine:
Blizzard Storm/DirectDraw 8-bit 2D engine, StarCraft and Brood War 1.16.1.
- StarCraft.exe (md5 50d53a3b...) is identical in the root and in BroodWar\.
- storm.dll (md5 76a285e2...) is identical in both too.
- Each game mounts its own disc image from _disc\ with Daemon Tools.
titles.launch_sets:
Always 640x480x8 exclusive DirectDraw.
- StarCraft.exe asks for SetDisplayMode(640,480,8) at 0x41da48.
- Only if that fails does it fall back, at 0x41da6c, to SetDisplayMode(GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN), GetSystemMetrics(SM_CYSCREEN), 8): the desktop size at 8 bpp. This is not user-selectable.
- Neither launcher has FLEETRES, and none applies.
- How a 640x480 mode appears on the 16:9 panel (stretched or pillarboxed) depends on the GPU and monitor scaler. It is UNKNOWN: GDI only ever sees the 640x480 surface, and nobody has looked at the screens.

CHANGED from the prior answer: .123 is no longer excluded.
- HWPROFILE on .123 reports disc_mount=true (evidence 'd347bus', Daemon Tools 3.47; daemon.exe is running).
- .123's All Users desktop carries StarCraft.lnk and 'StarCraft - Brood War.lnk', written by tonight's GAMESYNC at 2026-09-29 03:47 UTC.
- Whether StarCraft actually runs on .123 is untested.
titles.menu_source:
There is no resolution option.
- The only requested mode is the immediate 640x480x8, plus the desktop-size fallback that fires only on failure.
- The storm.dll display init is called with 640x480 (0x41d528).
- install.reg and FLEET-NOTES.txt confirm there is no windowed mode. The only switches in the binary are ddemulate and nosound.
titles.evidence:
Static (re-disassembled independently):
- StarCraft.exe 0x41da3b: push 8; push 0x1e0; push 0x280; call [ecx+0x54].
- On failure, 0x41da4f loads GetSystemMetrics (IAT 0x4fe368). Then: push 0 -> SM_CXSCREEN, push 1 -> SM_CYSCREEN, push 8, call [edx+0x54] at 0x41da6c.
- The prior agent searched only for the byte pattern 'ff 51 54', so it missed this 'ff 52 54' site.

Mounter and shortcuts on .123:
- /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/rts2d-review/hwprofile_123.json: disc_mount=true (d347bus).
- Agent DIRLIST of .123's All Users desktop shows both StarCraft shortcuts.

The bogus compat row:
- /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/rts2d-static/240_StarCraft_Play_StarCraft.png shows the Daemon Tools error 'Unable to mount image. Unit is locked.', not the game.

- Resolution Expander / InsectLoader / ResSettings: not found (case-insensitive) under Files/Game Updates, Patches, Utility and Games-Library/_patches.
titles.fix:
None possible: StarCraft 1.16.1 hard-codes a 640x480x8 request and has no video-mode setting.

Alternatives, none of them an in-game option:
- Blizzard's free 1.18+ patch and Remastered need Windows 7+ (Remastered also a DX11-class GPU) and are not LAN-compatible with 1.16.1 peers.
- The Resolution Expander injector is not on the share.
- cnc-ddraw 6.6.0.0 on the share could rescale the 640x480 surface through its ddraw.ini (maintas / fullscreen). That is not an in-game option, and it would ship a game-local ddraw.dll to every box.

titles.title: WarcraftOrcsAndHumans
titles.engine:
DOS WAR.EXE (DOS4GW LE, GOG 1.2) in VGA mode 13h (320x200x256).
- Re-checked: exactly one 'mov eax,13h; int 10h' at file offset 0x3474f, and no VESA 4F02h anywhere.
- Runs under GOG's DOSBox 0.74-2.1 (DOSBox.exe md5 2318a446..., SDL.dll md5 b8b92fee...). Daggerfall and MOO2 ship the same build.
- That build offers the surface, overlay, opengl, openglnb and ddraw outputs.
titles.launch_sets:
The defect is real and was reproduced on hardware today.
- With the deployed conf (output=surface, fullresolution=desktop), WC1 shows an unscaled 640x480 frame at (640,300)-(1280,780) of the 1920x1080 panel.
- Seen on .145 (XP) and .195 (Win7): EVR/wc1_145_A_deployed_surface.png and wc1_195_A_deployed_surface.png.
- Cause: DOSBox's surface output cannot scale. Its own help text says 'try an output different from surface' and 'output=surface does not!' [support hardware scaling].
- The launchers (FLEETRES -ini dosboxWC1.conf sdl fullresolution %FR_DOSFULLRES%) and GAMERES (gameres.h:799) handle fullresolution correctly.
- The .240 caveat (no EDID, so 'original') is stale. GAMERES on .240 now reports dosbox_fullresolution=desktop.
titles.menu_source: There is no resolution option. The game is a 1994 320x200 VGA title that sets mode 13h and never calls VESA. How it fills the panel is decided only by DOSBox's [sdl] output settings.
titles.evidence:
EVR = /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/rts2d-review/

titles.title: Postal
titles.engine:
Running With Scissors' SDL2 rebuild, 'POSTAL Classic and Uncut' (GOG).
- Postal.exe md5 986a6395..., PE subsystem 5.1, imports only KERNEL32 and SDL2.
- It needs SSE2. All four LCD boxes have it (Athlon 64 on .123 and .240, i5-2400 on .145 and .195, per docs/fleet-inventory.md).
- It renders an 8-bit frame, converted into an ARGB8888 streaming texture (SDL_CreateTexture format 0x16362004) through SDL_Renderer.
titles.launch_sets:
Hardware-verified on .240. This was the title's first launch on any box.
- The 'Postal' SDL_app window is at 0,0-1920x1080 and in the foreground.
- The desktop mode stays at 1920x1080x32, so this is fullscreen-desktop with no mode switch, as the binary predicts.

CORRECTION to the prior agent:
- The title screen, main menu and options screens are 640x480 art pillarboxed to 1440x1080 in the centre of the panel (content x=239..1679), with black bars about 240 px on each side. They do not fill the panel.
- The game's UI code centres 640-wide elements with (w-640)/2 (e.g. at 0x42b61b). Only the gameplay view uses the full 853x480 logical frame, and gameplay was not observed.

The size follows the LIVE desktop (SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode):
- All four LCD boxes have a persisted desktop of 1920x1080 today (GAMERES).
- docs/fleet-inventory.md still says 1024x768 for .145, which is stale.
- The launcher CALLs FLEETRES.BAT but writes nothing, which is correct.
titles.menu_source:
There is no resolution option. Confirmed on hardware.
- Main menu: START / OPTIONS / EXIT.
- OPTIONS: AUDIO, CONTROLS, PERFORMANCE, DIFFICULTY and GAME. There is NO 'VIDEO' entry here, which corrects the prior agent's 'OPTIONS -> VIDEO -> GAMMA'.
- PERFORMANCE: TRANSPARENCY, 3D LIGHTING, PARTICLES, DYNAMIC VOLUME, AMBIENT SOUNDS.
- GAME: COAT COLOR, CROSSHAIR.
- The VIDEO/GAMMA strings do exist in the exe, probably in the in-game Esc menu (not observed).
- The only size control is the '-resolution WxH' command line, which makes a real SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN window of that size. The internal frame stays (desktop_w*480/desktop_h) x 480.
- rspSetVideoMode (0x42fc50) never reads its depth, device-width or device-height arguments, so POSTAL.INI's DeviceWidth, DeviceHeight and UseCurrentDeviceDimensions have no effect on the window.
